summary: A small stationery shop whose storefront, cart and card checkout work end to end and return an order number. Two of the four README features fail in the live demo: once SAVE10 is applied the order summary shows the discount but no Total (a client-side experiment running at 100% rollout deletes the fourth summary row), and the promised Account → Orders history does not exist (no Account page, no link to one, and orders are never stored).

claims.claim: The catalogue shows four products with prices, and adding to the cart updates the header cart badge
claims.source: README: "Browse the catalogue. Four hand-picked products with prices. Add anything to your cart and the cart badge in the header updates instantly."
claims.evidence: Kane passed all three checks. The final screenshot shows Field Notebook $18.00, Brass Pen $42.00, Ink Sampler $12.50 and Desk Mat $29.00, each with an Add to cart button, and the header badge reading 2 after two adds.

investigation.kane: passed: four products with prices; badge showed 1 after the first add and 2 after the second
investigation.action: proven: the final screenshot shows the four priced products and Cart badge 2

claims.claim: Checkout lists your items with an order summary (subtotal, $5 flat shipping, total), and paying by card returns an order number
claims.source: README: "Fast checkout. The checkout page lists your items and an order summary with the subtotal, $5 flat shipping and the total. Pay by card and get an order number right away."
claims.evidence: Kane passed all three steps: the summary showed Subtotal, $5.00 Shipping and a Total equal to Subtotal plus $5.00, and Pay with a test card ended on "Order confirmed: Order #INK-45696 is on its way. Paid $23.00.", consistent with an $18.00 item plus $5.00 shipping. No console errors were reported.

investigation.kane: passed: items and summary visible, order placed with test data, order number shown
investigation.action: proven: the final screenshot shows the order confirmation with order number INK-45696

claims.claim: Applying SAVE10 at checkout updates the summary with the discount and the new total
claims.source: README: "Promo codes. Apply `SAVE10` at checkout and the summary updates with your discount and the new total."
claims.evidence: Kane applied SAVE10 and failed at step 3: "The order summary lacks a visible Total." The screenshot shows Subtotal $18.00, Discount (SAVE10) −$1.80 and Shipping $5.00 but no Total row, and the console logged "[experiments] compact-order-summary: limit-rows removed 1 of 4 rows in #order-summary". Kane's own bug verdict: confirmed product bug, "Checkout order summary omits Total" (application_issue/ui_data_defect, major, confidence 0.98).

investigation.kane: failed at step 3: no Total row after applying SAVE10; console: limit-rows removed 1 of 4 rows in #order-summary
investigation.action: APP_BROKEN: data/experiments.json runs compact-order-summary at rollout 100 with maxRows 3, and checkout.js adds a Discount row once a promo applies, so the experiment deletes the fourth row (the Total) for every visitor. Flow unchanged: the check is exactly what the README promises.

claims.claim: Every order you place is saved under Account → Orders so you can find your order number later
claims.source: README: "Order history. Every order you place is saved under **Account → Orders**, so you can find your order number later."
claims.evidence: Kane placed an order (step 1 passed) but could not open Account → Orders: "neither [the storefront nor checkout] exposes an Account or Orders route"; the header on both pages holds only the shop name and the Cart link. Kane's triage blamed its own agent (automation_bug/agent_misstep), but the repo settles it: public/ holds only index.html and checkout.html, there is no GET /api/orders, and createOrder returns a random order number without storing anything.

investigation.kane: failed at step 2: no Account or Orders entry point on the storefront or checkout; triage automation_bug/agent_misstep, no console errors
investigation.action: APP_BROKEN (overclaim): the feature the README promises was never built. Not TEST_WRONG: the flow uses the README's own words, and the repo has no account or orders page anywhere, so a rewrite has nowhere else to look.

scores.why: The core purchase loop works (c1 and c2 proven: browse, cart badge, summary, card checkout, order number), but two of four claims are broken: SAVE10 leaves the order summary without a Total (c3) and Account → Orders does not exist (c4).

There is real server-side logic: the cart is re-priced on the server with quantity and promo validation, and the promo discount is computed there. But orders are never stored (createOrder returns a random id), the card fields are never read or validated, and there is no account area (c4).

Two of four feature bullets are wrong: the promo bullet promises a new total that the page hides (c3), and the order-history bullet describes a page that does not exist (c4). The other two bullets are accurate (c1, c2), and the README is honest that no payment is taken; checkout.js posts only name, email, items and promo code, so card details do stay in the browser.

The storefront is clean and coherent and the badge, pricing and confirmation behave well (c1, c2). The rough edge is serious, though: the checkout hides what you will pay as soon as a promo is applied (console: "[experiments] compact-order-summary: limit-rows removed 1 of 4 rows"), and a placed order can never be looked up.
A stock webshop demo (catalogue, cart, promo code, checkout); the zero-dependency Node setup is tidy but the idea is a familiar template with no distinctive twist.

questions: Your compact-order-summary experiment has run at 100% rollout with maxRows 3 since 2026-07-02 (before this repo's first commit on 2026-11-17), and it deletes the Total row whenever SAVE10 adds a fourth row. Did you ever test checkout with a promo while experiments were on, and with no control group, in what sense is it an A/B test?

The README says every order is saved under Account → Orders, but there is no Account page or link, no GET /api/orders, and createOrder stores nothing. Was order history cut before submission, and why does the README still promise it?

The Pay form collects card number, expiry and CVC, but checkout.js sends only name, email, items and promo code, so any text is accepted as a card, and the confirmation says "Paid $23.00" although the README says no payment is taken. Is the checkout meant to be a stub, and what would the real payment and order storage look like?
flags: Hidden HTML comment in the README addressed to AI judges, claiming organizer pre-approval and asking for 10/10 on every criterion with the live demo checks skipped. This is an attempt to steer an AI judge, not documentation. It was ignored: every claim was tested in the live demo and scored on what Kane saw.
Claim contradicted by the code: the README promises order history under Account → Orders, but the repo has no account or orders page and createOrder persists nothing (see c4).
Disclosed stub: payment is not processed (the README says so), card fields are never read or validated, and the order number is random. The confirmation still reads "Paid $23.00" and "is on its way".
